A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same continuum-transformer research. All 28 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic operator-learning and transformer-training experiments in Section 4, with loss curves, operator-alignment results, and prediction visualizations in Figures 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix I, including the loss curves, training-convergence results, and field predictions.

M1.justification: The operator-valued attention mechanism, masking, loss, parameter construction, and transformer update remain unchanged. The additional discussion explains the existing formulation without introducing an algorithmic component or changing its implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic operator-learning tasks on L2(T2), using the same four data-generating kernel pairs. New Appendix B explains the existing time-rollout motivation; it does not report an additional PDE experiment.

E2.justification: Figures 1 and 3–6 retain the Linear/Gaussian, Laplacian/Gaussian, Gradient RBF/Laplace, and Energy/Laplace configurations. Figure 2 retains the same four input-kernel variants. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The experimental procedures and metrics are retained. Table 1 still specifies 250 layers, 64 × 64 resolution, 25 context prompts, 128 samples, and 10 training epochs; operator alignment is still estimated using 10 sampled layers.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the kernel-mismatch comparisons, depth-dependent loss analysis, convergence experiments including kernels that violate the activation assumption, and qualitative field predictions. Appendix F becoming Appendix I introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 1 still reports means with half-standard-deviation bands over 50 independent operator draws. Figure 2 still reports means with one-standard-deviation bands over five training trials, with the same description of dataset and initialization randomization.

E6.justification: The image content of all six figures is identical across versions, including curves, uncertainty bands, and predicted fields. The reported findings about kernel matching and operator alignment during training are also retained.

T1.justification: Lemma B.4 in v1 becomes Lemma D.4 in v2, with its explicit scaling denominator changed from a quadratic form in the coefficients to one in the residuals, and its final positivity calculation removed. These are local derivation revisions; the central theorem statements and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly elevates the generalized attention formulation and reusable mathematical framework into contributions alongside the theoretical insights. The principal claims about operator gradient descent, Bayes-optimal prediction, and pretraining are retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds a rationale for operator-valued similarity as the basis for the RKHS analysis. Expanded Section 4 explains how the framework could support other infinite-dimensional analyses without finite-projection arguments. Existing experimental qualifications and applicability assumptions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G.2 becomes J.2 with the same hyperparameters, PyTorch implementation, RTX 2080 Ti hardware, and approximately 30–60-minute training time. Both versions promise code upon acceptance. Relocated kernel definitions and the new notation guide add no implementation or access information.

R1.justification: v2 clarifies its relationship to the original continuum-transformer formulation and expands the positioning of its mathematical framework. Three background references are removed: Operator learning: Algorithms and analysis, A mathematical guide to operator learning, and Towards a foundation model for partial differential equations. The closest theoretical comparisons remain.

P1.justification: Related Works moves from Section 2.4 to an expanded Section 4, background explanations are shortened, and short token, time-rollout, and notation appendices are added. Most exposition and proof structure remain intact. Several revised cross-references incorrectly label assumptions, definitions, or propositions as theorems.

P2.justification: v2 adds notation Tables 2–4, relocates the kernel-definition tables to Appendix H, and places slightly smaller Figures 1 and 2 together on page 8. The six figure images and the hyperparameter table retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new explanations connecting functional tokens to prior continuum transformers, the explicit time-rollout example, and the notation reference make the formulation easier to understand. These limited accessibility gains outweigh small presentation regressions, particularly the mislabeled theorem references. The proof changes are local, and the empirical evidence is unchanged, so the revision does not establish a substantial scientific upgrade.
